title: Beijing Lu Xun Museum
geometryBasis: OpenStreetMap way 447939893 names the museum grounds. Overture-derived building roofs set the axes and approximate positions of the historic north and south sides and the east exhibition pavilion. The former residence point was checked independently against the named map record.
sectionBasis: Beijing’s cultural heritage office records a small preserved courtyard house with three bays to north and south and two per side. The museum’s own research office gives the layout and area of the rear writing room. Shizhao’s Qualla original shows the historic threshold and No. 21 plaque. EditQ’s two exact public-domain dedications show the exterior court of the permanent exhibition and its three-bay glazed pavilion.
limitations: The rooms are placed according to the museum’s documented order, the mapped roof axes and the distinct location pin for the former residence. House bay dimensions, rear fence, roof profiles and subdivision of shared neighborhood roofprints are approximate.

The standing east exhibition pavilion follows its mapped roofprint and the two 2023 creator-released exterior photos. Details of its back, steps and interior facings are simplified. The separate eastern buildings, interiors, decorative inscriptions and sculpture are outside the modeled scope.
